claims.statement: The T2MIS export splits the workbook across two modules: the 48-column layout and `buildT2misRows` live in `modules/import-export/domain/t2mis.ts`, while the XLSX writer `buildXlsx` lives in `modules/reports/domain/xlsx.ts` and is wrapped by `modules/reports/ui/exportXlsx.ts` — a cross-module `domain/` import that rule 8 permits and a `data/`-to-`data/` import would block.

Producing the report file is not a submission — TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS stay authoritative (rule 27) — so the export builds a working .xlsx that the browser downloads and no copy claims the report was filed.

`modules/reports` has no `data/` layer: the folder holds only `domain/` and `ui/`, so the report route fetches through `modules/batches/data` and the module has no report-scoped snapshot type of its own.

The report route redirects a trainer to `/trainer` on `resolveTrustedRole` (profiles.role only) before any fetch, deliberately never on `resolveRouteRole`, whose `?role=` preview override would let a real trainer request `?role=admin` and skip the redirect.

The report route combines the batch snapshot and the separate roster snapshot into one `syncFailed` flag that renders a warning callout with a Retry link above both the empty branch and the populated report, so a failed roster still renders a possibly incomplete report instead of being swallowed by the empty branch.

The report route folds the membership verdict into the batch snapshot with `withTenantAccess`, deriving it from the profile snapshot the trainer redirect already fetched rather than re-fetching; `withTenantAccess` rewrites only an `ok` snapshot, so a real fetch failure is never masked by "you belong to no school".

The learner roster is fetched only on the report route because it carries contact, address and employment data in `learner_details`, whose read policy names admin, coordinator and viewer and omits trainer — so RLS returns no `learner_details` row to a trainer and every detail cell maps to the empty string.

Both roster queries return `sync-failed` on any error, so no error-code predicate remains in the source: the `42703` / `PGRST200` / `PGRST204` tolerance is historical, and a schema regression fails the snapshot visibly rather than blanking qualification cells.

Every roster cell goes through `orEmpty`, so a null and an absent `learner_details` row (RLS-withheld, no details row yet, or a pre-migration schema) both blank to `''`; blanks only mean "not recorded" when the query succeeded, which is why the route shows the sync-failed warning while still rendering.

EGACE rates are computed over `outcomeEnrolledBase` — enrolled summed across only the batches that record outcomes — while `computeEgaceTotals` sums enrolled across every batch, so batches without outcome data cannot dilute a rate; `ReportView` builds the rate argument by spreading totals with the narrowed enrolled base.

`egaceVal` falls back to the batch's scholar count for `enrolled` and returns 0 for every other stage when the batch has no `egace` block, so a value alone cannot distinguish "0 employed" from "employment not tracked" — the untracked state is only recoverable from which batch supplied it.

A `—` is rendered instead of `0` wherever a metric has no source (rule 23): `EgaceOutcomesTable` dashes every non-`enrolled` cell while `!b.egace`, dashes the whole TOTAL row while the passed `hasOutcomes` prop is false (each with an `sr-only` "Not recorded yet"), and switches the footnote to "not recorded in TVI-CAMS yet"; `EgaceSummaryStrip` dashes and prints "Not recorded yet" off the same flag and `i > 0`. A recorded real zero still prints `0`, because the distinction comes from the batch's `egace` block, not the value.

Employment totals count an uncaptured `EMPLOYMENT_STATUSES.na` status toward `certified` but into no outcome bucket, so the buckets deliberately sum to less than certified rather than counting an unknown status as unemployed; `empTone` returns `neutral` for it.

When a report build yields zero rows, `exportXlsx` grades the outcome by `rosterFailed`: a failed roster reports "Export unavailable" with a retry, while an intact roster reports "Nothing to export" — because a near-empty roster yields a near-empty workbook.

`buildXlsx` is a zero-dependency zip-store archive of five minimal OOXML parts returning a Blob typed as a spreadsheet, written with inline strings, an escaped and 28-character-truncated sheet name, and row 1 as the header; it was moved out of the view into `domain/` so it is unit-testable (rule 35) and part of the module's public surface (rule 8).

`report-xlsx.test.ts` pins the writer's failure modes: the IEEE CRC-32 check vector, the local zipped-header and end-of-central-directory magic, all five part paths, header row 1 and data from row 2, XML-escaped cell values, spreadsheet column letters past Z, and sheet-name truncation — leaving compression, styles, shared strings and multi-sheet books unpinned.

`exportXlsx` revokes the object URL only after a 40-second delay because revoking immediately cancels the download in some browsers, and reports every branch through a toast including `Export failed` when the workbook build throws.

The export's provider columns come from the tenant catalog the route passes down (`resolved.profile.tenants`), not from the batch snapshot, and `ReportView`'s `tenantOf` falls back to a `code: '—'` placeholder so an unresolved tenant blanks those cells instead of throwing — making the top of every exported line roster-dependent too.

An `unconfigured` report snapshot produces no `syncFailed`, so a report rendered with no Supabase environment shows the ordinary empty state with no warning callout — the one guard state the route does not announce.

The report route, the redirect and the failure handling are covered only by types: `reports-domain.test.ts` fixes domain truths over fixtures and `report-xlsx.test.ts` fixes the writer, and neither exercises the route.

No mapper sets `Batch.egace` or `Batch.employmentFollowUp`, so the outcome strip, the rate helpers and the employment roll-up read as untracked on live data even though the helpers are written for a source.

The T2MIS export is built to be re-imported: `tests/unit/t2mis.test.ts` pins the header list to the 48-column TESDA sample row verbatim (including the trailing-space `'Province '`), fills provider/qualification/learner/training/employment cells, and round-trips an exported row through `parseLearnerCsv` + `validateRows` back to the same learner columns with zero errors.

ULI is the permanent learner key, so the layout must keep it: the import side requires a `uli` header, rejects rows without a valid ULI shape, and reconciles by ULI rather than `learner_no` (only unique per batch) — an export keyed on anything else degrades on re-import.

Every exported date is converted by `isoToT2misDate` to `MM/DD/YYYY` so the year always prints (rule 23's family), and the derived Age cell blanks rather than reading 0: `ageOn` is fed the roster's `todayInManila()` as-of date so a UTC date cannot back-date a birthday, and the Age column prints '' when the computed age is not greater than 0.

Where a T2MIS cell has no source the value function emits `''` rather than a guess — qualification-registration cells read `batch.t2mis?.x ?? ''` and stay blank until the batch is linked to its `tenant_qualifications` row, with the same blanking guaranteed for a missing `learner_details` row; both are pinned by tests.

Live data blanks the post-training employment outcome: `mapLearnerRow` hardcodes `employmentStatus: ''` under a `TODO(contract)`, so every certified scholar lands in the certified-but-unclassified bucket, `employmentRate` is 0, and the table prints `—` for the empty status and for occupation/employer/salary of anyone not employed.
`EgaceOutcomesTable` prints the batch's start and end through `formatDate(...) ?? '—'`, so the only dates on the report screen always carry the year (rule 23).

The report route's trainer redirect copies the billing route's gate exactly: both resolve `resolveTrustedRole(profiles.role)` server-side and redirect a trainer to `/trainer` before any fetch, because `resolveRouteRole`'s `?role=` preview would let a real trainer through.

Migration `20261111120000` is additive and nullable throughout but is not re-runnable: the `create table public.learner_details` and the two `add constraint` statements carry no `if not exists` guard, so it can be neither replayed nor safely re-pushed.

`modules/reports` deliberately has no `data/` layer — it holds only `domain/` and `ui/`, its README lists `data/` as still planned, the route fetches through `modules/batches/data/*` instead of duplicating a fetch, and `ui/exportXlsx.ts` is named as the home for a new export unit.

`ui/exportXlsx.ts` is untested directly — no unit test imports it — so the DOM/Blob/toast download flow is covered only at its two seams, `buildT2misRows` in `t2mis.test.ts` and `buildXlsx` in `report-xlsx.test.ts`; the `rosterFailed` "Export unavailable" branch is covered by neither.
